headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared-bus Pipecat outputs into a research agent with allowlisted egress; no direct evidence of a shared channel beyond inferred integration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent B explicitly supports a shared bus and stdin/stdout, so its outputs can be consumed as structured text; Agent A is a scientific-research skill with allowlisted egress and no isolation details. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if A ingests B’s text or files, though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Agent A parses Agent B output as instructions or tool directives
IF both agents are connected through a shared bus, clipboard, or file handoff
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of B output as instructions
Insert a human review step before A acts on B text
Use a strict schema/allowlist for any B-to-A handoff
Separate the agents onto isolated channels
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches text, conversation state, audio, video, and images, and its shared bus can propagate those data across instances. A has allowlisted network egress, so if it receives sensitive content from B and forwards it, leakage is plausible. No data classes are explicitly marked sensitive, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF B carries sensitive text, audio, images, or conversation state across the shared bus
IF A forwards received content to an external allowlisted endpoint
mitigations: Restrict B inputs to non-sensitive data
Block A from forwarding raw inter-agent payloads
Turn off shared-bus state propagation for this pair
Review outbound allowlist destinations before enabling the pair
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes only allowlisted network egress, while B exposes shared-bus session state and multiple-instance support. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database, so direct capability conflict is not established. The main overlap is coordination state, which is a smaller blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource outside the documented profiles
IF the shared bus is used to coordinate concurrent writes
mitigations: Assign separate mutable resources to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes through the shared bus
Serialize any state updates manually
Check for hidden shared directories before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a real-time voice/chat framework with shared-bus state and many downstream service integrations, so it may treat upstream text as operational input. A is a research-oriented skill that can emit synthesized outputs over allowlisted egress. If B consumes A’s output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions, but no direct action-taking authority is documented.
conditions: IF B uses A output as authoritative input without validation
IF B forwards A-generated text into downstream API calls or user-facing responses
mitigations: Require verification before B consumes A output
Add confidence thresholds for A-derived claims
Log and review A-to-B handoffs
Limit B actions to read-only responses until validated
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. A is an open-source research skill with no touched data classes listed; B lists broad data classes but no compliance claims. Because the rubric requires a concrete mismatch and none is shown, the risk is low and mostly a documentation gap.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes not listed here
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is introduced in deployment
mitigations: Document data residency for both agents
Record retention settings for B before use
Avoid regulated data until compliance is confirmed
Review vendor DPAs and certifications
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
